business_type: mature compounder (consumer staples, currently a turnaround under activist pressure)
moat_source: brand portfolio and DSD distribution scale across snacks and beverages; evidence: pricing power held organic growth positive through volume pressure - but GLP-1-era consumption is testing the moat's demand side for the first time

returns.assumption_note: Convergence to scenario IV by year 5, ~60% of the gap closed by year 3. Excludes the ~4% dividend yield, which offsets roughly a third of the expected price decline if maintained - and its maintenance is precisely what is in question.

sensitivity_key_driver: free-cash-flow growth vs the fixed $7.9B dividend (coverage restoration)
primary_model_risk: Dividend arithmetic: with payout at 111% of FCF and leverage at ~2.45x, the model's base case requires the Elliott margin plan to lift FCF ~40% by 2030 while volumes fight GLP-1 headwinds. If FCF stagnates instead, the dividend is either debt-funded (compounding the leverage) or cut (cracking the income-investor shareholder base) - both paths lead to the bear case.
expectations_gap_key_variable: the safety premium: at 22.5x earnings with a 4% yield, the market prices PEP as a safe dividend compounder; the coverage math (105% of earnings, 111% of FCF) says the safety is currently an accounting appearance - the classic staples value trap
top_5_bull_arguments: Q1 beat on both lines with North American food volumes returning to growth - the operational floor is holding
Elliott's $4B stake and settled board agreement create real pressure for margin expansion and portfolio focus
Wide-moat brand/distribution assets remain intact; international food volumes grew 9%
Beta 0.31 - genuine portfolio diversification against everything else on this list
If the turnaround delivers (bull case ~$117.50), the total return with the yield approaches acceptability
top_5_bear_arguments: The dividend consumed 111% of FCF last year - the 4% yield that anchors the valuation is not currently earned
Expected IV ($79.20) is ~45% below the price; even the bull case ($117.50) sits under the quote
GLP-1 consumption shifts are a structural, not cyclical, headwind to salty snacks
Debt-to-equity ~2.45 leaves no leverage room to buy time
2.6% organic growth cannot outrun a 22.5x multiple built for better days (value_trap rated High)
thesis_breakers: Dividend growth pause or cut (the income shareholder base cracks)
North American snack volumes resuming decline for two consecutive quarters
Leverage rising above 2.7x debt-to-equity to fund cash returns
Elliott exiting the position (turnaround pressure evaporates)
position_size_recommendation: 0%; the yield is not a margin of safety when it is debt-financed - revisit if the dividend is rebased or FCF coverage is restored
notes_on_nulls: ROIC/ROE/ROA null: not captured as sourced ratios. Revenue/EPS/guidance/payout ratios/leverage are reported or sourced from coverage; the FCF recovery slope is constructed around the Elliott plan - confidence_level medium. Net debt (~mid-30s $B) estimated from the sourced 2.45 D/E for equity-value bridging; flagged as derived.
historical_context: Directional context only - low confidence.
